name: Quignam
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Extinct, unclassifiable north-Peruvian coastal language; Glottolog lists no descriptive references; attested mainly in names/numerals.

new_statements.quote: From the alternation of vowels in the second syllable of trisyllabic terms with zero, it can be inferred that the penultimate was not stress-bearing in trisyllabic items in Quingnam. [...] In the few cases where it is marked, it invariably falls on the ultima. With the exception of <hórgamo>, the name of a plant used in curing, the same is true of lexical items with a possible Quingnam origin in the various sources discussed above. Taken together, the evidence thus points to a prosodic system in which stress (whatever its precise phonetic correlates) fell on the last syllable lexically.
new_statements.citation: Urban, Matthias. 2019. Lost Languages of the Peruvian North Coast. Estudios Indiana 12. Berlin: Ibero-Amerikanisches Institut / Gebr. Mann Verlag. DOI 10.57727/898
new_statements.locator: Chapter VII 'Quingnam', phonology sketch, subsection 'Stress', p. 172 (PDF page 173 of the saved file)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (314 pp., pdfinfo; title pages read: Matthias Urban, Lost Languages of the Peruvian North Coast, Estudios Indiana 12, IAI / Gebr. Mann, Berlin). extracted text of PDF page 173 carries the running head "172 VII. Quingnam" and a subsection headed "Stress" whose text matches the reported quote word for word, including "it can be inferred that the penultimate was not stress-bearing in trisyllabic items in Quingnam", "In the few cases where it is marked, it invariably falls on the ultima", "With the exception of <hórgamo>, the name of a plant used in curing", and "stress (whatever its precise phonetic correlates) fell on the last syllable lexically"; the [...] in the report correctly elid…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Where colonial scribes marked an accent on Quingnam names and the few possibly-Quingnam lexical items, it always falls on the last syllable; vowel~zero alternation in the penult of trisyllables shows the penult was unstressed. Urban infers word stress on the final syllable, adding that this 'may have been a general rule, or it may have occurred at least under certain conditions which cannot be recovered anymore' (p. 172).
new_statements.exceptions: <hórgamo> (name of a plant used in curing) is the one non-final case among possibly-Quingnam items; Urban hedges that final stress may have held only under unrecoverable conditions. Elsewhere (p. 87) he notes consistent final stress in regional-Spanish items in <-ó> (<cagaló>, <chinguió>, <crespió>, <incaló>) and (p. 148) that final stress in <patà> 'is not suggestive of a Mochica'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, but the evidence is entirely indirect: orthographic accent marks on 16th-17th-century personal names and toponyms from the Moche/Chicama valleys plus a handful of lexical items in Spanish sources; no speaker data, no citation forms, no phonetic correlates. Contrasts with Mochica, for which final stress is posited by no interpreter (Urban p. 124).
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog's 'Quignam' = the language usually called Quingnam (Calancha 1638), also 'lengua pescadora'/'Pescadora' and loosely 'Chimú'; Urban 2019 treats Pescadora as identical to or a dialect of Quingnam, and Salas García 2010 argues the two names refer to the same language. Urban's stress inference draws on names from the Moche and Chicama valleys (Trujillo) and a few Chicama/Jequetepeque items; no dialects are distinguished. Language is extinct (last references mid-18th c.), so the statement is a philological reconstruction, not a description of speech.

VII Quingnam, 'Stress', p. 172 (PDF p. 173): stress rarely marked in the colonial data, but where marked 'it invariably falls on the ultima'; same for possibly-Quingnam lexical items except <hórgamo>; penult not stress-bearing in trisyllables (vowel~zero alternation); evidence points to lexical stress on the last syllable, perhaps a general rule or only under unrecoverable conditions; contrasts with Mochica where no interpreter posits final stress.
EN: 'Word-final stress' among distinctive features (phonology section drawn from Urban 2019); ES: words typically stressed on the last syllable. Tertiary; used only to build the bibliography.

sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: For Mochica, not Quingnam; but section 9.2 (p. 353) treats final accent as a diagnostic of non-Mochica (possibly Quingnam) origin: 'The final accent is not typical in Mochica at all, its presence in these assumed Mochica words [<lapà>, <munà>, <patà>] makes me think that they are foreign words and that they could be of Quingnam origin'. Second-hand corroboration of final stress as a Quingnam trait.
